item.description: Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine student and aspiring dermatologist Arianna Falletta believes that beyond science, medicine is about supporting people.

item.description: School of Architecture and Design students are recognized for their academic work at MIT’s Reality Hack and in Metropolis magazine’s Future100.

item.title: Op-ed: The College Degree Isn’t Dead. But the Wrong Kind Could Cost You $2 Million.
item.description: A Fortune op-ed by President Jerry Balentine, D.O., contends that universities built for the next decade must prepare graduates to move beyond technical execution and develop skills AI can’t replicate.

item.title: New York Tech Launches Civil Engineering Degree Program
item.description: The new degree program will prepare graduates to address critical infrastructure needs that directly enhance communities and the built environment.

item.description: During a semester-long design studio project, two architecture students discovered their appreciation for community and their place in their future profession.

item.title: Student Wins Best Presentation in Puerto Rico
item.description: Life sciences/osteopathic medicine student Talia Lilikakis traveled to Puerto Rico for the Annual Meeting of the Society of Thoracic Radiology, where she won Best Student Oral Scientific Presentation.

item.title: Examining the Role of Inequality in Human Migration
item.description: Mathematical models fall short in their predictions of migration. Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering Alain Boldini, Ph.D., seeks to improve these models by including conflicts, natural disasters, and economic factors.
